findings.claim: No test checks that only car 0's finish saves racer.finished.<id>. If the save fired on any racer's finish, a bot crossing the line on Hay Loop would unlock Pine Ridge, and every test would still pass. The spec says "A player finish saves the key", and AC6 says "When car 0 finishes".
findings.evidence: Mutation: change line 199 `if (!finished && r.world.racers[0]?.finishTick != null) saveFinished(r.track.id);` to `if (r.world.racers.some((x) => x.finishTick != null)) saveFinished(r.track.id);`. Every test that touches the key calls `finishRace` (tests/game/pine-ridge-helpers.ts:800). It plays `twinPlayerInputs` until car 0 finishes and then asserts car 0 finished, so the key is set under both the real code and the mutant. The Dust Bowl case (pine-ridge-unlock.test.ts:942) saves 'dust-bowl' under both. No test runs a Hay Loop race where a bot finishes and the player doesn't and then checks that localStorage has no racer.finished.hay-loop.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test in a new file, e.g. tests/game/pine-ridge-player-only.test.ts. Use setup(), then `game.startRace({ trackId: 'hay-loop', seed: 3, carCount: 2 })`. Play NO_INPUT-equivalent inputs (e.g. `game.play(Array(10800).fill({steer:0,throttle:0,...}))`) until `state().race.racers[1].finishTick` is set, with racers[0].finishTick still null. Then assert `localStorage.getItem('racer.finished.hay-loop')` is null and the Pine Ridge card is still aria-disabled after game.showMenu().

findings.claim: No test covers select() re-reading the lock. That is the path where the menu comes back after a race on a track that unlocked after the menu last showed. If the re-read were removed, quitting to the menu after racing Pine Ridge would leave it unselected, and RACE would start a different track. The tests would still pass.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete line 362 `if (card) card.setLocked(locked(trackId));`. Sequence: new game with empty storage, so the Pine Ridge card has locked=true from the constructor's refresh(). Call finishRace(game,'hay-loop'), which saves the key, then game.startRace({trackId:'forest-ridge'}), or reach it via NEXT RACE from Dust Bowl, with no menu show in between. Then game.showMenu() (game.ts:310) calls startScreen.select('forest-ridge') before show(). Under the mutant, pick() sees the stale `locked === true` and returns, so the checked radio stays Bramble Bends, and RACE starts 'bends' instead of 'forest-ridge'. AC7's test (pine-ridge-unlock.test.ts:950) goes NEXT RACE from hay-loop, which wraps to 'bends', and picks Pine Ridge by click after show(). It never runs select() on the just-unlocked id, so the mutant survives.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test, e.g. in a new tests/game/pine-ridge-menu-return.test.ts: setup(); finishRace(game,'hay-loop'); finishRace(game,'dust-bowl'); click 'Next race' and expect trackId 'forest-ridge'; press Escape, then click 'Quit to menu'. Assert checked(root) contains 'Pine Ridge' and that clicking 'Race' starts 'forest-ridge'.

checked.how: Read the assertions. AC1 pins the name, laps, width, validateTrack on the raw JSON, the TRACKS order and the exact TRACK_LOCKS. AC2 checks corners with a greedy turn window and a 40-unit gap, and checks self-overlap over all sample pairs more than 60 units apart. AC3 checks the tree count against every other track, trees on both sides by cross-product sign, and prop clearance. No trivial asserts.
Seeds 1–3, 6 bots including car 0, a 10800-tick cap, and it asserts every racer has a finishTick and lapsCompleted 3. A bot that can't finish would fail it.

Mutations: dropping `id === currentId ||` makes nextTrackId('forest-ridge') throw, which is caught. Returning true in hasFinished's catch is caught by the throwing-getItem case. Not filtering locked tracks is caught by the dust-bowl→hay-loop case.

Removing the pick() guard (start-screen.ts:304) is caught by the click test. Removing the initial refresh() is caught by the aria-disabled check. Changing `locked ? null : bestMs` in track-card is caught by the stored-best test. Removing the arrow-skip loop is caught by Dust Bowl→Hay Loop.

Moving saveFinished to showMenu is caught by the results-screen storage check. Removing refresh() from show() is caught by AC7. Saving the wrong id is caught by the Dust Bowl case. A save on a bot finish is not caught (F1).
NEXT RACE goes through the real button in both lock states. With blocked storage, removing the try/catch in saveFinished/hasFinished would throw inside finishRace or the menu render, so it's caught.

Both stages are checked for aria-disabled and the padlock. The Chromium test checks that 4 radios and RACE are in the viewport and don't overlap, and checks the clip on leaf spans. The name and best spans are flex items of the column plate, so they're blockified and clientWidth is meaningful.
Grep in game.ts: select(menuTrack.id) at :310 runs before show() at :311, so select's lock re-read is load-bearing and untested (F2).
